questions.prompt: Several independent Claude Agent SDK subagents run concurrently. How long do they take, per the docs?

options.text: The sum of all of their individual times.
options.explanation: That is the time when they run one after another.

options.text: The time of the slowest one.
options.explanation: Right. The docs say independent subtasks finish in the time of the slowest one rather than the sum.

options.text: The average of their individual times.
options.explanation: The wait ends when the last worker is done, not at the average.

questions.prompt: A team runs the same security review prompt on a diff three times and flags any run that finds a problem. Which Anthropic variation is this?

options.text: Sectioning, which breaks the task into independent parts.
options.explanation: That splits one task into different subtasks. Here the same task is repeated.

options.text: Voting, which runs the same task several times.
options.explanation: Right. The Anthropic engineering post defines voting as running the same task multiple times to get diverse outputs.

options.text: Orchestrator-workers, where a model decides the subtasks.
options.explanation: Nothing here decides subtasks at run time. The same prompt simply runs again.

questions.prompt: Which Python primitive does the OpenAI Agents SDK orchestration page name for running agents in parallel?

options.text: A `while` loop that runs an evaluator agent after each task.
options.explanation: That is the evaluator pattern. It repeats work in sequence, not in parallel.

options.text: A structured output that picks the next agent by its category.
options.explanation: That is routing: one agent is chosen, so nothing runs in parallel.

options.text: `asyncio.gather`, for tasks that do not depend on each other.
options.explanation: Right. The docs name it as a way to run multiple agents in parallel for speed.
